A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TGR work, with matching methods and main experiments, and their supplied contents are readable. V1 ends after the references despite unresolved appendix references; v3 includes Appendices A–H. This is an identifiable difference in supplied content, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and code-generation evaluations, component ablations, inference-scaling results, and comparisons across training stages in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds controlled sensitivity experiments, further baseline comparisons, open-ended evaluations, and quantitative geometry and efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: The default anchor sampling, geometric scoring, residual injection, and chunk-wise inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendices A.5 and C.9 add optional multiple-rollout scoring and top-two candidate reevaluation, evaluated in Table 8. These are limited procedural extensions; the expanded initialization and implementation descriptions do not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluated instruction-following and generative-writing tasks through IFEval and the Literature & Arts subset of WritingBench (Appendix D.3, Table 12). This substantially broadens task coverage beyond v1’s retained mathematics and code-generation benchmarks.

E2.justification: V1 cites ToT and GoT but reports TGR-Token as its token-space control, without separate results for those methods. V3 directly evaluates ToT and GoT against TGR on AIME25 and HumanEval in Table 11, materially strengthening the comparator coverage for its central latent-versus-token search comparison. Existing main-table comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds a controlled chunk-length experiment with S = 256, 512, and 1024 while holding L×S = 12288 fixed, latent-interface and rollout-strategy sweeps, and Self-BLEU@32 evaluation for the new pilot tasks. These introduce additional experimental designs and metrics. The retained main experiments keep their stated default settings; newly disclosed implementation details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and rollout-depth/candidate-budget sensitivity plots, v3 adds chunk-length and latent-interface sensitivity tests, hard-filter feasibility measurements, selected-versus-rejected anchor diagnostics, quantitative collapse/cycling analyses, and overhead decomposition. Tables 4, 6, 8, 13, and 14 and Figure 7 substantially expand evidence about stability, mechanisms, and computational costs.

E5.justification: V1 already displays ±1σ uncertainty bands in Figure 4. V3 newly specifies three independent runs with seeds 42, 1234, and 3407, adds dispersion summaries in Table 13, and reports IQR across hyperparameter settings in Figure 13. This expands statistical documentation without establishing that the number of runs increased; the main result tables still lack uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. V3 adds extensive results across model scales, additional comparators, pilot tasks, sensitivity settings, and geometry/efficiency diagnostics. Examples include TGR AUCs of 78.6 on IFEval and 63.6 on WritingBench, and hard-filter acceptance of 28.5% at 1.7B versus less than 1.5% at 14B. These are newly reported results, not improvements over matched v1 measurements.

T1.justification: V1 provides an acceptance-rate definition and qualitative scaling arguments. Appendix B adds explicit runtime and KV-memory derivations, including the approximate 1 + Ks/S forward-token multiplier, and a spherical-cap concentration heuristic for exponential acceptance decay. Appendix E formally specifies candidate-diversity statistics, including spectral-entropy effective set size. This substantially expands mathematical support, although the concentration argument is explicitly heuristic.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: training-free manifold-informed latent search, bounded KV memory, improved trajectory coverage with up to 13-point AUC gains and approximately 1.1–1.3× overhead, and poor scaling of hard geometric filtering. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability and failure discussions. Section 5.3 identifies hidden-state access requirements and the limitation for closed-box APIs; Appendix A explains the fixed random interface’s perturbative role; Appendix H discusses over-regularization, candidate collapse, and loss of exact information under aggressive KV resets. It also interprets the newly tested chunk-length trade-off between control frequency and overhead.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C supply implementation information missing from v1’s unresolved appendix references: Gaussian initialization, normalized hidden states for bumpiness, proposal radius 0.05, score weights 0.5, prefix-cache reuse, batched rollouts, and explicit accounting for rollout and cache-rebuilding tokens. These materially improve reproducibility documentation without proving that previously used settings changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for IFEval and WritingBench and briefly positions TGR as complementary to KV-cache compression and retention methods in Appendix B.2. The existing related-work sections and principal positioning against sampling, RL, and geometric approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The original section order and most main-text prose are retained. Changes include capitalization, affiliation and publication-header information, a conflict disclosure, resolved cross-references, short robustness and applicability additions, and an appendix roadmap. The substantial scientific additions do not entail extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V3 retains the original main tables and figures while adding Table 4, appendix Tables 5–14, Figures 6–13, and a fuller inference algorithm display. New visualizations include geometry distributions, scoring box plots, scaling profiles, throughput comparisons, and stability plots. This substantially expands the presentation of evidence, beyond page-count growth or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 remedies an important deficiency in v1: implementation details and supporting analyses repeatedly referenced there were absent from the supplied paper. The appendices now provide substantial technical documentation, explicit derivations, controlled sensitivity tests, and direct ToT/GoT comparisons, improving reproducibility and scrutiny of the retained claims. Some additions remain weak: WritingBench’s pass criterion is unspecified, and Appendix G.1’s claimed successful example contains incorrect algebra. These temper confidence in those additions, while the overall gains in technical completeness and supporting validation remain substantial.
